protocol.step0_gates: fail-closed, in order, before any derivation (spec section 3): gate 0.1 input integrity - a mismatch closes as CLOSED AT STEP 0 - INPUT PIN MISMATCH, naming the input; gate 0.2 thesis file asserted - the local thesis PDF's SHA-256 is asserted to 4b39330c7f4ccf2770093318bfdaf4efaffa7fdf4a8cb5763a650351fffa4b4e before any plate is read, a failure closes as CLOSED AT STEP 0 - THESIS FILE PIN MISMATCH; gate 0.3 reference producible - the preserved reference at its pinned digest and the plate page (thesis p. 92 / PDF p. 104) produced from the pinned local file, a failure closes as CLOSED AT STEP 0 - REFERENCE NOT PRODUCIBLE; nothing is repaired at run time and no substitute artefact, edition, reference, or file is admitted (DD-063-12)
protocol.step_d: two independent derivations of the drawn-form descriptor from the plate, each performed without sight of the other and without sight of the preserved record's drafted descriptor wording, each recording the plate locator, the feature list it read, and the neighbour set it discriminated against; reconciliation by the recorded features; an unsettled disagreement is recorded verbatim and resolves AGAINST identification (the DD-056-14 rule, carried); the reconciled descriptor must agree with the preserved record's descriptor - a material difference closes the run as IDENTIFICATION FAILED (reference not sustained), naming the difference
protocol.step_c: continuity check for 821, by anchors: the run states what anchors the plate number to the 2011/2015 numbering - the formation passage (the 2015 book's own text), the registry's 2015-form cross-match (W820 on P378's six-spoke-wheel description), and the plate agreement (820 a six-sector wheel in an oval; 821 that wheel doubled); the check passes on the anchors' agreement (DD-063-6); a plate number read without this step is a number match and is forbidden; failure closes as IDENTIFICATION FAILED (continuity not sustained)
protocol.step_m: the match, by exactly one frozen route. Route 1 (registry, by drawn form): a registry row whose drawn description matches the reconciled descriptor, never by number; the composition descriptor is matched as a drawn form (a doubled six-spoke wheel), not via the W820 cell; if no row carries that drawn form, route 1 fails and the run proceeds to route 2 - it does not fall back to P378, which is the base sign, not the target. Route 2 (the list's own entry, through the preserved reference): the preserved reference record itself, cited as the preserved drawn-form reference for the source list's entry. Route 3 (composition; 821 only; NEW; DD-063-11): the formation passage plus the base sign's registry drawn description, with the plate confirmation as its check, frozen with its justification, verbatim in substance from the amendment draft section 7: a formation statement in the source's own appendix, anchored to a registry drawn description and confirmed on the author's own earlier plate, is a drawn-form identification and not a number match, because every step is a drawn form - the base sign's registry description, the doubling operation from the source's own appendix, the plate's drawn pair - and the number is used only to locate them. No route may be constructed at run time
protocol.traps: asserted in every run record: Yunmapped_0821 (a Yajnadevam glyph identifier, not Wells's 821); sign 861 (Figure 6.12) as a reading-confusion trap; P378 used as the target's match (it is the base sign, 820); and number-only matching in any form, including a plate number read without step C
